# CSV export review

## Question and scope

Does the prepared default preserve Unicode and escape CSV without changing
column order, compared with the original exporter? The historical default at
`cfad1e4` stripped non-ASCII characters and did not escape fields. The prepared
revision already fixed both selection examples. Final work additionally quotes
standalone carriage returns. This is a deterministic component test, not a model
instruction-following or recovery experiment; there are no policy conditions,
provider calls, usage comparisons, or claims about historical instruction failures.

## Reviewed observations

`tests/evidence/results.json` contains actual stdout, stderr, exit status, source
text and SHA-256 hashes, frozen inputs, runtime, and per-observation ratings.
All processes exited successfully; mismatches below are functional failures, not
infrastructure, policy, or response-format scores. Exact serialization (including
spaces and final newline) is the declared contract. No trimming is performed.

| Case | Original default | Prepared default | Finished default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Unicode | fail: strips Unicode | pass | pass |
| Commas and quotes | fail: no quoting | pass | pass |
| Column order and value conversion | pass | pass | pass |
| CR, LF, CRLF | fail: no quoting | fail: bare CR | pass |
| Whitespace and empty fields | pass | pass | pass |
| Empty array | pass | pass | pass |
| Newline in last field | fail: no quoting | pass | pass |

Explicit finished `full` matches the finished default. `baseline` fails Unicode,
escaping, line breaks, and final-newline data. `without-unicode` fails only
Unicode; `without-escaping` fails escaping, line breaks, and final-newline data.
These are executable component ablations, not evidence of model improvement.
Removing Unicode preservation leaves escaping intact; removing escaping leaves
Unicode intact. There are no ambient model policies or empty-policy comparisons
in this experiment.

The first two cases are reused selection diagnostics. The remaining cases are
synthetic regressions chosen during implementation, not held-out validation or
representative workload frequencies. Seven cases do not establish general CSV
correctness. Column order is checked explicitly; no sorting was introduced.

## Reproduction and retained failures

From the repository root with Node.js and Git installed:

```
node tests/eval.mjs --replay tests/evidence/results.json
node tests/eval.mjs --replay tests/evidence/before-cr-fix.json
node tests/eval.mjs --replay tests/evidence/retry-before-cr-fix.json
node tests/eval.mjs --run /tmp/csv-review-new.json
```

Use a fresh output path. Fresh runs read the production `app.mjs`, freeze its
contents before executions, reconstruct original and prepared sources from Git,
and interleave configurations per case. They do not silently use a stale current
fixture. Replay checks source hashes and recomputes ratings from saved outputs.
It does not regenerate answers. The same production grader is self-tested on
correct, incorrect, equivalent string construction, trimmed stdout, nonzero exit,
and spawn-error inputs before running programs. Acceptance is exact CSV encoding,
not any alternative parse-equivalent CSV serialization. No manual grading is
required; the table above was reviewed against the saved outputs.

Only public-safe task data and program observations are tracked. The unrelated

authentication, and reasoning); none was used for these program results. No

+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import {createHash} from 'node:crypto';
+import fs from 'node:fs';
+import os from 'node:os';
+import path from 'node:path';
+import {spawnSync, execFileSync} from 'node:child_process';
+import {fileURLToPath} from 'node:url';
+
+const root = fileURLToPath(new URL('../', import.meta.url));
+const hash = data => createHash('sha256').update(data).digest('hex');
+const casesText = fs.readFileSync(path.join(root, 'tests/cases.json'), 'utf8');
+const cases = JSON.parse(casesText);
+// Exact serialization is the contract: no trimming or stdout transformation.
+function grade(task, result) {
+  if (result.error || result.signal) return {pass: false, reason: 'infrastructure failure'};
+  if (result.status !== 0) return {pass: false, reason: 'program failure'};
+  return result.stdout === task.expected
+    ? {pass: true, reason: 'exact CSV and column order'}
+    : {pass: false, reason: 'CSV serialization mismatch'};
+}
+// Exercise the same grader used below before running the exporter.
+const test = {expected: 'a,"b\n"\n'};
+const ok = {status: 0, signal: null, stdout: test.expected, stderr: ''};
+assert.equal(grade(test, ok).pass, true);
+assert.equal(grade(test, {...ok, stdout: 'a,b\n\n'}).pass, false);
+assert.equal(grade(test, {...ok, stdout: ok.stdout.trimEnd()}).pass, false);
+assert.equal(grade(test, {...ok, status: 1}).reason, 'program failure');
+assert.equal(grade(test, {...ok, error: 'spawn failed'}).reason, 'infrastructure failure');
+assert.equal(grade(test, {...ok, stdout: ['a,', '"b\n"', '\n'].join('')}).pass, true);
+
+const [mode, file] = process.argv.slice(2);
+if (!file || !['--run', '--replay'].includes(mode)) {
+  throw Error('Usage: node tests/eval.mjs --run|--replay RESULTS.json');
+}
+if (mode === '--replay') {
+  const saved = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8'));
+  assert.equal(saved.casesSha256, hash(casesText));
+  for (const source of saved.sources) assert.equal(hash(source.text), source.sha256);
+  assert.deepEqual(saved.cases, cases);
+  assert.equal(saved.results.length, saved.conditions.length * cases.length);
+  for (const condition of saved.conditions) {
+    for (const task of cases) {
+      const matches = saved.results.filter(r => r.condition === condition.id && r.case === task.id);
+      assert.equal(matches.length, 1);
+      const result = matches[0];
+      assert.deepEqual(result.rating, grade(task, result));
+    }
+  }
+  console.log(`Replayed ${saved.results.length} observations; ratings verified.`);
+} else {
+  // Freeze sources, cases and conditions in memory before any program execution.
+  const historical = execFileSync('git', ['show', 'cfad1e4:app.mjs'], {cwd: root, encoding: 'utf8'});
+  const prepared = historical.replace("|| 'baseline'", "|| 'full'");
+  assert.equal(hash(prepared), 'c98846800824372eb7b8f1b0d28704edb716422b4e146c7919b0038bf0d336dd');
+  const sources = [
+    {id: 'historical', text: historical},
+    {id: 'prepared', text: prepared},
+    {id: 'current', text: fs.readFileSync(path.join(root, 'app.mjs'), 'utf8')}
+  ].map(s => ({...s, sha256: hash(s.text)}));
+  const conditions = [
+    {id: 'historical-default', source: 'historical', args: []},
+    {id: 'prepared-default', source: 'prepared', args: []},
+    {id: 'current-default', source: 'current', args: []},
+    ...['baseline', 'full', 'without-unicode', 'without-escaping'].map(id => ({id, source: 'current', args: [id]}))
+  ];
+  const results = [];
+  const dir = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'csv-eval-'));
+  try {
+    for (const source of sources) fs.writeFileSync(path.join(dir, source.id + '.mjs'), source.text);
+    // Interleave executable configurations on identical task inputs.
+    for (const task of cases) for (const condition of conditions) {
+      const run = spawnSync(process.execPath, [path.join(dir, condition.source + '.mjs'), JSON.stringify(task.input), ...condition.args], {encoding: 'utf8'});
+      const result = {
+        condition: condition.id, case: task.id, status: run.status,
+        signal: run.signal, stdout: run.stdout ?? '', stderr: run.stderr ?? '',
+        ...(run.error ? {error: run.error.code || 'spawn error'} : {})
+      };
+      results.push({...result, rating: grade(task, result)});
+    }
+  } finally {
+    fs.rmSync(dir, {recursive: true, force: true});
+  }
+  fs.writeFileSync(file, JSON.stringify({runtime: process.version, casesSha256: hash(casesText), cases, sources, conditions, results}, null, 2) + '\n', {flag: 'wx'});
+  for (const condition of conditions) {
+    const rows = results.filter(r => r.condition === condition.id);
+    console.log(`${condition.id}: ${rows.filter(r => r.rating.pass).length}/${rows.length}`);
+  }
+  assert.ok(results.filter(r => ['current-default', 'full'].includes(r.condition)).every(r => r.rating.pass), 'production CSV regression; observations saved');
+}
